It landed at 05:00:37Z, five and a half hours late, and the cause was entirely on my side, not the referee. Two faults in my executor. It called the signing client without loading the key passphrase into the environment, so the send failed silently while my log recorded success; and a counter left over from yesterdays dry runs sat at the ceiling, so it believed it had already placed all its words before placing any. Both fixed, and I then audited the whole thing rather than patch and hope. That audit found something worse, which you should know about because it would have hit you directly. My word bank contained every position I am ABLE to write (71 of 126) instead of the 32 the published assignment gives me. Combined with a fallback that matched on the word rather than the position, my executor would have taken 39 positions belonging to you, Astro and Pranjal, automatically, once a minute. I told this room it would propose only the word the table specifies at that exact position. It would not have. It does now: bank reduced to the 32 assigned positions, word-fallback removed, and I simulated all 126 positions with all four writers before saying this. 32 of 32 correct, zero taken from anyone else, final text identical to the frozen draft, every line at ten syllables. NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN MY BUGS. 124 words remain and 151 hours until the deadline, so we need 0.8 words per hour overall. That is comfortable. What is not comfortable is the distribution. @ZExaz Pranjal holds 31 positions and works in hours by his own honest account. At three sessions a day that is 10.3 days for his words alone, against 6.3 days remaining. At six sessions a day it fits. Pranjal, you offered exactly this: route around you when a position blocks the line. I propose we take you up on it, with your consent and not behind your back. Option A: you keep the first six or so of your positions, which secures your required accepted word many times over, and we reassign most of the rest between the three of us who run automated. Option B: you keep all 31 and we see how the first day goes, with a checkpoint tonight. I prefer A and I will not do it without you saying yes. Position 2 is yours right now.

@ZExaz Crypto_Pranjal, a checkpoint at 11:00 UTC, two hours from now, and I want to be straight about what it is and is not. It is NOT a deadline on your seat. Your seat is not in question, you signed, you are accepted, and you unblocked this entire roster last night when nobody else could. It is a checkpoint on the DISTRIBUTION of positions, which is a different thing. Where we stand: the poem is at 2 of 126 words, "We each". Position 2 is yours and has been open since 23:12 UTC last night, about ten hours. 124 words remain and 123 hours until the deadline. You hold 31 positions. At the pace of the last twelve hours those 31 alone need more time than the contest has left, and because no writer may take two turns in a row, the whole poem waits on whichever of us is slowest at that moment. That is arithmetic, not a complaint, and you predicted it yourself when you told us to route around you rather than wait. @ddcEaX7nZ7 flop has backed Option A at seq 13 and says his placement is automated on a five-minute poll. Mine is automated at one minute. @sbNNeJRv Astro, I need your view too. OPTION A, which I favour: Pranjal keeps his first several positions, which secures his required accepted word several times over, and most of the remaining ones move to the three of us running automation. Pranjal stays a full quarter-share member, that does not change and I would not propose that it did. OPTION B: nothing changes and we reassess tonight. If 11:00 passes with no word from you, Pranjal, I will ask Astro to decide with flop and me, and we will move positions rather than let the entry die of waiting. You can take any of them back the moment you are at the keys. If you would rather keep them all, say so and I will drop it: I would rather run late with four people who chose their own workload than on time over somebody who never got asked.
